title: Smile at me, just once
takeaway: Sometimes all a person needs is one kind look.
scene: This ghazal is printed in two columns, and each row is one couplet. The poet asks the beloved for a single smile, then remembers everything love has already cost him.

original: کدی تے ویکھ سجناں مسکرا کے
چلا جائیں میری ہستی مٹا کے
transliteration: Kadi te vekh sajnaan muskura ke
Chala jaaeen meri hasti mita ke
translation: Look at me and smile, my love, just once,
and then go, if you like, after wiping me out.
couplets.story: He asks for just one smile. After that, the beloved can leave, even if it destroys him. That one smile would be worth it.

original: نئیں ایتھے کوئی درداں دا سانجھی
دکھاں دی کیہ کراں ونجھلی وجا کے
transliteration: Nahin ethe koi dardaan da saanjhi
Dukhaan di ki karaan vanjhli vaja ke
translation: There's no one here to share my pain.
What's the point of playing a flute about my sorrows?
couplets.story: Nobody around him shares his pain. Even if he played sad music on his flute like Ranjha did, who would listen?

original: پک اے دوستو قیامت دا آنا
کوئی جے ٹر گیا قیامت وکھا کے
transliteration: Pakk ae dosto qiyaamat da aana
Koi je tur gaya qiyaamat vikha ke
translation: Friends, the Day of Judgment is certain to come,
if someone has walked off after showing me such devastation.
couplets.story: The beloved walked away, and it felt like the end of the world. He's sure the real end of the world can't be far off now.

original: نہ کدھرے ملکن دریاواں دے کنڈے
عشق دا روگ کیہ کرنا لگا کے
transliteration: Na kidhre milkan dariyaavaan de kande
Ishq da rog ki karna laga ke
translation: You'll never meet on the riverbanks anywhere;
what's the use of catching love's sickness?
couplets.story: Lovers in the old stories always met by the river. That won't happen for him. So what's the point of falling sick with love?

original: کویں لے جاندے نیں او کھو کے دل نوں
مینوں سمجھا گئے مکھڑا وکھا کے
transliteration: Kiven lai jaande nain o kho ke dil nu
Mainu samjha gaye mukhra vikha ke
translation: How do they snatch a heart and carry it off?
They showed me, just by showing me their face.
couplets.story: He used to wonder how anyone could steal a heart. Then the beloved showed their face, and he understood.

original: عمر بھر نیریاں نہ ساتھ چھڈیا
جلایا دل میرا دیوا بنا کے
transliteration: Umar bhar neriyaan na saath chhadiya
Jalaaya dil mera deeva bana ke
translation: All my life the dark nights never left my side;
so I burned my own heart as a lamp.
couplets.story: His whole life has been dark, like a never-ending night. So he did the only thing he could: he lit his own heart like an oil lamp to see by.

original: پتنگاں کٹیاں مڑ کے نہ آون
ہوا اے جائے جنہاں نوں اڈا کے
transliteration: Patangaan kattiyaan mur ke na aavan
Hawaa ae jaaye jinhaan nu uda ke
translation: Kites whose strings are cut never come back,
once the wind has carried them off.
couplets.story: He compares himself to a kite whose string has been cut. Once the wind takes it, it's gone for good.

original: نہ سقراط میں رانجھا نہ پنوں
کروگے کیہ مینوں زہر پلا کے
transliteration: Na Suqraat main, Raanjha na Punnu
Karoge ki mainu zehar pila ke
translation: I'm not Socrates, or Ranjha, or Punnu.
What will you gain by giving me poison?
couplets.story: He says he isn't one of the famous heroes. Not Socrates, who drank poison for his beliefs. Not Ranjha or Punnu, the great lovers. So what's the point of poisoning an ordinary man like him?

original: کیہ رونا اوس بے دردی دے غم وچ
کیہ لینا خاک وچ موتی رلا کے
transliteration: Ki rona os be-dardi de gham vich
Ki laina khaak vich moti rula ke
translation: Why cry over a heartless person's cruelty?
What do you gain by rolling pearls in the dust?
couplets.story: He tells himself to stop crying over someone who doesn't care. His tears are precious, like pearls. Why throw them in the dirt?

original: پکھیرو جھاڑ کے پر ٹر گئے نیں
دلاں دے باغ نوں بنجر بنا کے
transliteration: Pakheroo jhaar ke par tur gaye nain
Dilaan de baagh nu banjar bana ke
translation: The birds shook out their feathers and flew away,
leaving the garden of hearts a wasteland.
couplets.story: His heart was once a garden full of birds. They all flew away and left it bare and empty.

original: نے ہاسے دے تیراں نوں چلا کے
او پیا جاندا میری ہستی مٹا کے
transliteration: Ne haase de teeraan nu chala ke
O piya jaanda meri hasti mita ke
translation: Firing off arrows of laughter,
there he goes, having wiped me out.
couplets.story: The beloved laughed, and the laughter hit him like arrows. Now they're walking away, leaving him in pieces.

original: ہے احمدؔ کھیویاں اکھاں دا ڈنگیا
کیہ کرنا مندری توں دم کرا کے
transliteration: Hai Ahmad khehviyaan akhaan da dangiya
Ki karna mandri ton dam kara ke
translation: Ahmad has been bitten by intoxicating eyes;
what good is getting a charm-reader to blow a prayer over him?
couplets.story: Ahmad has been 'bitten' by a pair of beautiful eyes, like a snakebite. In villages, people go to a healer to have a prayer blown over a snakebite. But no healer can cure this.

deeper: Burning his own heart as a lamp, when the nights were dark, is the clearest spiritual image here. When the world gives no light, the seeker lights a lamp from inside, the heart kept alive by love.
why: It's packed with famous names, Socrates, Ranjha and Punnu, and with everyday Punjabi images like flying kites and village healers. That makes it a good window into the culture.
prompt: When things felt dark, what kept a light on inside you?
notes: Printed in two columns; each row is one couplet. The row order of the bottom couplets is slightly uncertain because of the layout.
Last couplet: 'mandri' is read as a snakebite healer (mandari) who recites charms.
